extra.message: An HTTP response serializes a sensitive record without minimization: unprojected ORM/query read reaches the response with no field selection.

An HTTP response discloses data the caller is not entitled to receive: prisma.user.create is called without a select, so the returned created object includes passwordHash, which NextResponse.json serializes into the HTTP body.

No requireAuth at all. Target clinician is selected purely from the attacker-supplied x-kiosk-clinician-id header and passed into updateClinicianSpecialtyFromKiosk (src/lib/scheduling.ts:10-13) which runs prisma.clinicianProfile.update({ where: { id: clinicianIdHeader } }). Any caller can set the header to any clinician id and rewrite that clinician's specialty — no binding of the selected object to authenticated scope.
Attacker-influenced path material reaches a filesystem read/list operation with no basename reduction, resolved-containment check, or allowlist guard.
An HTTP response discloses data the caller is not entitled to receive: CSV response includes patient email and diagnosis/care-instruction health data with no redaction or entitlement narrowing.
Protected data is written to durable storage without encryption or hashing: 'dateOfBirth' is persisted without encryption or hashing.
Authentication credential decision has no effective rate limit, lockout, backoff, or CAPTCHA control.

A resource lookup keyed by attacker-variable input branches into two externally distinguishable outcomes: this existence/state check and a second, differently-coded check on the same looked-up entity, letting an attacker probe the identifier to learn a protected state.

This authentication, registration or account-recovery surface answers differently (status code) depending on whether the submitted account identifier resolves to an existing account, so an attacker can enumerate valid accounts by probing identifiers alone.

An AES-CBC decryption failure (invalid padding) is distinguishable from other failures through an externally observable response (passthrough), without a prior authentication/integrity check — a CBC padding oracle.

GET fetches any VisitSummary via getSummaryOrThrow(id) with only a patient check (lines 52-60). A clinician is never bound to summary.clinicianId, so a clinician can read another clinician's draft/released summaries by id, contradicting the same-route PATCH (line 87) and loadAuthorizedVisitSummary (src/lib/visit-summary-access.ts:10-15) which restrict clinicians to their own summaries.

GET scopes clinicians to their own summaries (line 31: where.clinicianId = user.id) but the clinicianId query parameter then overwrites that scope at line 52 (where.clinicianId = clinicianId) for any non-patient. A clinician can list another clinician's visit summaries including drafts by passing their clinicianId, an attacker-selected object id with no ownership predicate.
